title: Sawyers et al. v. Missouri Presbytery
disposition_detail: Complaint found judicially in order; the SJC answered the issue “Yes” and found Missouri Presbytery erred under BCO 34-5 in its BCO 31-2 investigation by not finding a strong presumption of guilt that TE Jeffrey Meyers held views contrary to the Westminster Standards. Further action was held moot because MOP had already tried TE Meyers on April 13–14, 2012, so no remand or additional relief was ordered. Vote: 14 concurring, 1 dissenting, 3 recused, 6 absent.
first_summary: Elders complained that Missouri Presbytery erred in finding insufficient evidence to raise a strong presumption of guilt against TE Jeffrey Meyers for Federal Vision views. The SJC answered yes, finding MOP erred under BCO 34-5 in its BCO 31-2 investigation and remanding for compliance with BCO 31-2.
summary: Elders complained that Missouri Presbytery erred in its BCO 31-2 investigation by finding insufficient evidence to raise a strong presumption of guilt that TE Jeffrey Meyers held Federal Vision views contrary to the Westminster Standards. The SJC answered yes: MOP erred under BCO 34-5, and the ordinary remedy was compliance with BCO 31-2. But because MOP had already tried Meyers on April 13–14, 2012, the SJC held further action moot, ordering no additional relief. Adopted by the SJC as a whole, with one dissent.
